name: adopt
description: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.

name: architecture-decision
description: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.

name: architecture-review
description: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.

name: art-bible
description: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.

name: asset-audit
description: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.

name: asset-spec
description: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.

name: balance-check
description: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.

name: brainstorm
description: Guides the user through finding and choosing a game concept. Use when the user wants game ideas, a new concept, a game jam idea, or to explore other directions, including dropping the current idea and starting over.

name: bug-report
description: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.

name: bug-triage
description: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.

name: changelog
description: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.

name: code-review
description: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.

name: consistency-check
description: Scan GDDs against the entity registry for cross-document conflicts. Grep-first approach targets conflicting sections, different stats.

name: content-audit
description: Audit GDD content counts against what's implemented — planned vs built.

name: create-architecture
description: Author the architecture blueprint before code is written. Validates decisions against the pinned engine, flags knowledge gaps.

name: create-control-manifest
description: Builds a short list of must-do and never-do coding rules per system from accepted ADRs. Use when the user wants programmer rules or a cheat sheet from the ADRs, or needs it regenerated after ADR changes.

name: create-epics
description: Turns the GDDs and architecture into epics, one per architectural module. Use when the user wants to break the game into epics or plan the work before writing stories. Not for splitting one epic into stories.

name: create-stories
description: Breaks one epic into implementable stories with acceptance criteria. Use when the user wants stories for an epic or the next batch of work to build. Not for turning the whole design into epics.

name: day-one-patch
description: Day-one launch patch — focused fix for known issues found after gold master. Mini-sprint with QA gate and rollback.

name: design-review
description: Reviews one design document for completeness, internal consistency, implementability, and design standards. Before handing to programmers.

name: design-system
description: Section-by-section GDD authoring for one system — walks through each required section, cross-references dependencies.

name: dev-story
description: Implements one story in code with tests, following its ADRs. Use when the user says to build, implement or start working on a story. Not for checking readiness beforehand or closing the story after.

name: estimate
description: Estimate task effort from complexity, dependencies, velocity, risk. Structured estimate with confidence levels.

name: gate-check
description: Ready to advance between development phases? PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL with blockers and required artifacts. 'Can we move to production?'

name: help
description: What should I do next? Use when stuck or you don't know what to do.

name: hotfix
description: Emergency fix bypassing normal sprint process — hotfix branch, approvals tracked, backport verified, full audit trail.

name: launch-checklist
description: Launch readiness across every department: code, content, store, marketing, community, infrastructure, legal, go/no-go sign-offs.

name: localize
description: Localization pipeline — find hardcoded strings, extract string tables, cultural review, VO, RTL, enforce string freeze.

name: map-systems
description: Decompose a concept into individual systems, map dependencies, prioritize design order, create the systems index.

name: milestone-review
description: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.

name: onboard
description: Onboarding doc for a new contributor or agent — project state, conventions, priorities relevant to the specified role.

name: patch-notes
description: Player-facing patch notes from git history and changelogs. Translates developer language into player communication.

name: perf-profile
description: Performance profiling — find bottlenecks, measure against budgets, produce ranked optimization recommendations.

name: playtest-report
description: Structured playtest report template, or turn existing playtest notes into structured feedback.

name: project-stage-detect
description: Analyze project state, detect stage, identify gaps, recommend next steps. 'Where are we in development?'

name: propagate-design-change
description: Finds architecture decisions (ADRs) made stale by a changed GDD and walks through resolving each. Use when the user changed a number or rule in a GDD and asks which ADRs or architecture decisions are now out of date.

name: prototype
description: Concept prototype before GDDs — throwaway HTML, Engine or Paper build, PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL/NOT ASSESSED. After /brainstorm and /setup-engine.

name: qa-plan
description: QA test plan for a sprint — classifies stories by Logic/Integration/Visual/UI, covers automated tests, manual cases, smoke scope.

name: quick-design
description: Lightweight spec for small changes — tuning adjustments, minor mechanics. Embeds directly into stories; skips full GDD.

name: regression-suite
description: Map test coverage to GDD critical paths, find fixed bugs lacking regression tests, flag drift from new features.

name: release-checklist
description: Pre-release checklist — build verification, certification requirements, store metadata, launch readiness.

name: retrospective
description: Sprint or milestone retrospective from completed work, velocity, blockers. Actionable insights for the next iteration.

name: reverse-document
description: Generate missing design or architecture docs from existing implementation — works backwards from code and prototypes.

name: review-all-gdds
description: Holistic cross-GDD review — contradictions between systems, dominant strategies, economic imbalance, cognitive overload, pillar drift.

name: scope-check
description: Scope creep check — current scope versus the original plan. Flags additions, quantifies bloat, recommends cuts. 'Any scope creep?'

name: security-audit
description: Security audit — save tampering, cheat vectors, network exploits, data exposure, input validation. Before public or multiplayer release.

name: settings
description: View or change project config — effective merged values, or set locally in project.local.yaml.

name: setup-engine
description: Configure engine and version. Pins it in CLAUDE.md; WebSearch fills reference docs when the version is beyond LLM training data.

name: skill-improve
description: Improve a skill via a test-fix-retest loop — static checks, targeted fixes, keep or revert on score change.

name: skill-test
description: Validate skill files for structural compliance and behavioral correctness. Four modes: static linter, spec, category rubric, audit.

name: smoke-check
description: Critical-path smoke gate before QA hand-off — runs the automated suite. A failed check means the build is not QA-ready.

name: soak-test
description: Soak test protocol for extended play — what to observe and log for slow leaks, fatigue, late-appearing edge cases.

name: sprint-plan
description: New or updated sprint plan from the current milestone, completed work, and available capacity.

name: sprint-status
description: Fast, concise sprint snapshot — burndown and emerging risks for situational awareness. 'How is the sprint going?'

name: start
description: Guides a first-time user through onboarding and picks the right workflow. Use when the user is new, just cloned or installed the studio, has no idea or engine yet, asks where to begin, or wants to bring in an existing game.

name: story-done
description: Closes a finished story: verifies each acceptance criterion, checks for design or ADR deviations and updates its status. Use when the user says a story is done, finished or ready to close.

name: story-readiness
description: Checks whether a story is ready to implement: clear acceptance criteria, no open questions, valid ADR and dependencies. Use when the user asks if a story, or the sprint's stories, are ready to start or build.

name: team-audio
description: Orchestrate the audio team — audio-director, sound-designer, technical-artist, gameplay-programmer — direction through implementation.

name: team-combat
description: Orchestrate the combat team — game-designer, gameplay-programmer, ai-programmer, technical-artist, sound-designer, qa-tester — design through implement and validate.

name: team-level
description: Orchestrate the level team — level-designer, narrative-director, world-builder, art-director, systems-designer, qa-tester — for complete area creation.

name: team-live-ops
description: Orchestrate the live-ops team — live-ops-designer, economy-designer, analytics-engineer, community-manager, writer — for a season or live event.

name: team-narrative
description: Orchestrate the narrative team — narrative-director, writer, world-builder, level-designer — for story, world lore, narrative-driven levels.

name: team-polish
description: Orchestrate the polish team — performance-analyst, technical-artist, sound-designer, qa-tester — to optimize and harden a feature or area.

name: team-qa
description: Orchestrate the QA team through a full testing cycle — qa-lead strategy and test plan, qa-tester case writing, execution, sign-off.

name: team-release
description: Orchestrate the release team — release-manager, qa-lead, devops-engineer, producer — to execute a release from candidate to deployment.

name: team-ui
description: Orchestrate the UI team through the UX pipeline — authoring, visual design, implementation, review, polish. Uses /ux-design, /ux-review, studio templates.

name: tech-debt
description: Track, categorize and prioritize technical debt across the codebase — scans for debt indicators, maintains a register.

name: test-evidence-review
description: Quality review of test files and evidence — goes beyond existence, evaluates assertion coverage. ADEQUATE/INCOMPLETE/MISSING/NOT ASSESSED per story.

name: test-flakiness
description: Find flaky tests from CI logs — aggregates pass rates, spots intermittent failures, recommends quarantine. After multiple runs.

name: test-helpers
description: Generate engine-specific test helper libraries — assertion utilities, factory functions, mocks in the engine's test folder. Reduces boilerplate.

name: test-setup
description: Scaffold the test framework and CI — tests/ directory, engine test runner, GitHub Actions workflow. Once, before the first sprint.

name: ux-design
description: Section-by-section UX spec authoring for a screen, flow or HUD. Reads the player journey to provide context; also project-wide accessibility.

name: ux-review
description: Validate a UX spec, HUD design or pattern library — accessibility, GDD alignment, readiness. APPROVED / NOT ASSESSED / NEEDS REVISION / MAJOR REVISION NEEDED.

name: vertical-slice
description: Pre-production validation — end-to-end build to confirm the full loop is achievable before committing to Production. After GDDs, architecture, UX specs.
